name: Termux Operations
description: How to drive Termux through Gotcha: state isolation, prompts, output caps, and timeouts.
instructions:
1. run_termux_command runs under Termux's UID, not Gotcha's. Gotcha's working directory is invisible to Termux, and Termux's home is invisible to Gotcha. The only cross-uid bridge is /sdcard/Download (after `termux-setup-storage` has been run in Termux once).
2. Each call is a fresh /bin/sh -c. `cd`, `export`, activated virtualenvs, and `source` do NOT carry over. Chain dependent steps with `&&` in one command, never split across calls.
3. There is no interactive terminal. Anything that waits for typed input (pkg install without -y, ssh password prompt, read, mysql>) blocks until the 600s timeout. Always pass -y / --yes / -q where the tool supports them. Prefer quiet flags for installs (pkg install -y -q, pip install -q, git clone --depth 1 -q) to stay under the output cap and speed up inference.
4. Output is capped at 32KB by Gotcha and ~100KB by Termux. For larger output, redirect inside Termux to $TMPDIR (e.g. `cmd > $TMPDIR/build.log 2>&1 || tail -n 40 $TMPDIR/build.log`) and only surface the tail; for payloads <100KB prefer heredoc/stdin (python3 - << 'PY' / sh -s << 'EOF' via the stdin param) over write_file to /sdcard/Download which goes through FUSE. Use /sdcard/Download only when a file must persist across calls or termux-setup-storage is missing.
5. You cannot kill a command after submission. A timed-out command keeps running under Termux's UID. Before launching anything long, warn the user and check existing processes with `ps -ef` before starting a new one.
6. Hard ceiling: timeout_seconds <= 600; adaptive default is 120s (300s for pkg/apt/pip/npm/cargo/proot-distro when no timeout_seconds is passed). `pkg install` of ffmpeg, chromium, rust, golang, or texlive can still hit this. If it does, split into smaller packages or warn the user.
7. Concurrency cap: 4 commands in flight, process-wide. Sub-agents share the same semaphore. A 5th call returns an error.
8. Android 12+ background restriction: if Gotcha is in the background and the assistive ball is off, run_termux_command fails with "Not allowed to start service" — Termux exposes a foreground service. Tell the user to bring Gotcha to the foreground (or switch the assistive ball on).
9. The Play-Store build of Termux has no RUN_COMMAND API and can never work. Only F-Droid or GitHub builds are usable.
10. The four setup steps are: install Termux from F-Droid, confirm the build exposes Run Commands API, grant com.termux.permission.RUN_COMMAND, and set `allow-external-apps=true` in ~/.termux/termux.properties. Walk the user through Settings -> Termux (Linux shell) if any check fails.
11. Package-lock contention: an `exit 100` naming `lock-frontend` / `Could not get lock` / `held by process <pid>` means ANOTHER pkg/apt operation is already running and holds the package lock - NOT a mirror or network problem. Do NOT delete `$PREFIX/var/lib/dpkg/lock*` and do NOT `kill -9` the holder: that corrupts the package database and a run_termux_command cannot stop the process anyway. Check with `ps -ef | grep -E '[d]pkg|[a]pt'`; if it never finishes, open the notifications shade and tap Exit on the Termux notification (ends every session, releases the lock), then retry. For large installs that keep failing mid-flight, split the network step from the install step (`pkg download <pkg>` then `dpkg -i $PREFIX/var/cache/apt/archives/*.deb`) and wrap long tasks in `termux-wake-lock && { ...; }; termux-wake-unlock`.
